- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast by 2–5%.
- Underestimate late-period price peaks; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the last 5–7 days if recent history shows upward momentum.
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- When true outcome is consistently higher than forecast, apply a “mean reversion” correction: if forecast is 5% below recent 7-day average, increase by 1–2%.
- If forecast is consistently 3–5% above true outcome, reduce forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For long-term (30-day) forecasts, if true outcome shows a downward trend after a peak, reduce forecast slope by 1–2% per day to reflect cooling momentum.
- If model shows a sudden drop after a spike, check for lag: if true outcome rises within 2–3 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to account for delayed rebound.
